page: Microsoft Azure D192ds_v7 is a general-purpose virtual machine built on Microsoft Hyper-V virtualization. The instance features a 96-core Intel Xeon 6973P-C processor with multithreading enabled to deliver 192 dedicated vCPUs operating at 4.2 GHz. The hardware architecture incorporates 48 KB of L1 data cache per core, 2 MB of L2 cache per core, and a substantial 480 MB shared L3 cache. It includes advanced instruction sets including AVX-512, AMX Tile, and AMX INT8 for vectorized operations and matrix math. The platform includes 768.0 GB of RAM, adhering to a balanced 1:4 core-to-memory allocation (4.0 GB per vCPU), and integrates 11,340 GB of fast local NVMe SSD storage. It operates without a discrete GPU accelerator.

Benchmark evaluations highlight exceptional parallel processing and memory throughput. Multi-core performance is situated in the top tier across tests, reflected by a multi-core stress-ng result of 190,542.4 and top-tier PassMark CPU, encryption, and extended instruction scores. Memory bandwidth reaches 13,906.45 GB/sec for small cached blocks and 677.36 GB/sec for large uncached reads. The platform also exhibits top-tier I/O and web serving capabilities, yielding 158.23 GB/sec in static web throughput, 34,547.24 in PassMark database operations, and 250.73 million operations per second during Redis SET benchmarks.

The primary architectural tradeoff is the disparity between single-core and multi-core efficiency. While multi-threaded throughput is top tier, single-core stress-ng results place in the middle 50 percent, meaning non-parallelized workloads cannot fully leverage the underlying silicon. In addition, large language model prompt processing is capable on this hardware, but sequential token generation remains modest due to the absence of dedicated GPU accelerators. From a resource-density perspective, the machine consolidates immense compute and local NVMe capacity into a single footprint, making it a viable configuration for massive transactional databases, distributed in-memory caching tiers, large-scale data transformation, and highly parallelized batch analytics.
description: Microsoft Azure D192ds_v7 is a high-density general-purpose virtual machine designed for compute-intensive and I/O-heavy enterprise operations. Powered by a 96-core Intel Xeon 6973P-C processor running at 4.2 GHz, it provides 192 dedicated vCPUs with 480 MB of L3 cache, along with Advanced Matrix Extensions and AVX-512 instruction support. The instance is paired with 768 GB of system memory, matching a standard 1:4 vCPU-to-memory ratio, and includes 11,340 GB of integrated high-speed local NVMe SSD storage. Benchmark results place its multi-core processing, encryption, and static web throughput in the top ten percent of evaluated instances, accompanied by exceptional Redis caching performance exceeding 250 million operations per second. However, single-core processing metrics remain average, indicating that performance gains depend heavily on parallelization. Lacking dedicated GPUs, CPU-based text generation remains constrained. This virtual machine is best suited for large-scale distributed caching, transactional databases, and parallelized compilation or data-processing pipelines.
